title: The Hijra to Madinah
year: 622 CE — Year 1 of the Islamic Calendar
teaser: They plotted to kill him on the night he was to leave. He recited a verse of Surah Ya-Sin and walked past them unseen.

layers.title: The Decision to Kill
layers.subtitle: The plot at Dar an-Nadwa
layers.content:
When the Quraysh realized that the Prophet ﷺ had followers in Madinah and that the Muslims were quietly emigrating there, they convened an emergency meeting at Dar an-Nadwa — the House of Assembly.

They discussed three options: imprisonment, exile, or death. Abu Jahl proposed the solution they accepted: choose one young man from each tribe, give each a sword, and have them strike simultaneously. That way, the blood guilt would be spread across all tribes and the Banu Hashim could not retaliate against any one clan.

Jibreel came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of the plot. He was told: do not sleep in your bed tonight. The Prophet asked Ali to sleep in his bed and cover himself with the Prophet's green Hadhrami cloak, to protect the people's property that had been entrusted to the Prophet ﷺ.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 8:30 — 'And remember when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you or kill you or drive you out'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Night of Departure
layers.subtitle: He walked past them and they did not see
layers.content:
The assassins surrounded the house. They waited through the night for the Prophet ﷺ to emerge.

The Prophet ﷺ took a handful of earth and recited the opening verses of Surah Ya-Sin: 'And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see.' (36:9) He threw the earth over their heads and walked through them. Not one of them saw him.

When dawn came and they finally entered, they found Ali in the Prophet's bed. Their plot had failed entirely.

The Prophet ﷺ met Abu Bakr and they left together through a southern route, hiding for three days in the Cave of Thawr while the Quraysh searched for them with a reward of 100 camels.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 36:9 — 'And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Cave of Thawr
layers.subtitle: Abu Bakr's fear and the Prophet's certainty
layers.content:
In the Cave of Thawr, the searchers came so close that Abu Bakr whispered: 'O Messenger of Allah, if one of them looks at his feet he will see us.'

The Prophet replied: 'O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when Allah is their third?'

A spider had spun a web across the cave entrance. A pigeon had built its nest there. The searchers looked and turned away — the web appeared undisturbed, the nest untouched.

For three days they remained. Asma bint Abi Bakr brought them food. Abdullah bin Abi Bakr brought news of Makkah at night. When the searchers had finally dispersed, Abdullah bin Uraiqit came with two camels and they began the journey to Madinah.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 9:40 — 'Do not grieve — Allah is with us'
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when Allah is their third?' — Sahih Al-Bukhari
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Arrival in Madinah
layers.subtitle: The city that came out to greet him
layers.content:
When the Prophet ﷺ entered Madinah, the people came out to receive him. The women and children sang: 'The full moon has risen over us from the valley of Wada' — and we must show gratitude where the call to Allah is made.'

Every house of the Ansar wanted the Prophet to stay with them. He said: 'Leave her — she is commanded.' His camel, Qaswa, kept moving until she knelt of her own accord near the land of Banu Najjar. That was where the Prophet's Masjid would be built.

He asked who owned the land. It belonged to two orphan boys. He purchased it at full price and construction of the Masjid began immediately. He himself carried bricks alongside his Companions.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 22:41 — 'Those who, if We give them authority in the land, establish prayer and give zakah'
layers.hadith_ref: Narrated by Ibn Ishaq — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: Why the Hijra is the beginning of Islamic time
layers.content:
The Hijra is not merely a historical event — it is the pivot of Islamic civilisation. When Umar ibn al-Khattab later established the Islamic calendar, the Companions chose the Hijra as Year 1. Not the birth of the Prophet ﷺ. Not the first revelation. The Hijra.

Because the Hijra was when Islam moved from a message to a community. From a voice to a society. From persecution to the beginning of a state.

And the Hijra established a principle that has guided Muslims ever since: when you cannot practise Islam where you are, you move toward where you can. The Prophet ﷺ did not stay in Makkah and accept the limitations. He migrated — and the migration was counted by Allah as a sacrifice so great that those who made it were given a special title: Al-Muhajirun, the Emigrants.

And those who received them were given an equal title: Al-Ansar, the Helpers.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 4:100 — 'Whoever emigrates in the cause of Allah will find on the earth many locations and abundance'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

quiz.prompt: What plan did the Quraysh adopt to kill the Prophet ﷺ?

options.text: One assassin to strike at night
Poison his food
One young man from each tribe to strike simultaneously
Exile him to the desert

quiz.scholar_reflection: By spreading the blood guilt across all tribes, they hoped the Banu Hashim could not seek retaliation against any single clan.

quiz.prompt: Who slept in the Prophet's bed the night he left Makkah?

options.text: Abu Bakr
Zayd bin Harithah
Ali ibn Abi Talib
Abdullah bin Masud

quiz.scholar_reflection: Ali wore the Prophet's green Hadhrami cloak and slept in his bed, protecting the property entrusted to the Prophet ﷺ and deceiving the assassins.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ say to Abu Bakr when he feared they would be discovered in the cave?

options.text: Have trust in Allah, He will not abandon us
O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when Allah is their third?
Be still — they cannot hear us
Make du'a and Allah will send us help

quiz.citation: Sahih Al-Bukhari — narrated in the account of the Hijra
quiz.scholar_reflection: Not comfort. Certainty. There were three in that cave — and the third was Allah.

quiz.prompt: How did the Prophet ﷺ choose where to build his Masjid in Madinah?

options.text: He asked the Ansar to suggest the best location
He chose the highest point in Madinah
He let his camel walk freely and built where she knelt
Jibreel showed him the location in a dream

quiz.citation: Narrated by Ibn Ishaq — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: He said: Leave her — she is commanded. The camel's choice was not random. And the Prophet purchased the land at full price from the orphan boys who owned it.

quiz.prompt: Why did the Islamic calendar begin with the Hijra rather than the Prophet's birth or the first revelation?

options.text: The Companions simply chose that year arbitrarily
Because the Hijra was when Islam moved from a message to a functioning community
Because the exact dates of the birth and first revelation were unknown
Because Umar ibn al-Khattab was born that year

quiz.citation: Historical account — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: Umar ibn al-Khattab established the calendar. The Companions chose the Hijra because it marked the moment Islam became a society, not just a message.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet ﷺ walked past armed men who intended to kill him and they did not see him. How do you understand divine protection operating through seemingly natural means?

options.text: Allah uses the created world to protect what He wills
The Quranic verse he recited was the mechanism — not a coincidence
What appears miraculous is often simply Allah's will operating at a level we cannot perceive
All of these point to the same reality

quiz.citation: Quran 36:9 — the verse he recited leaving Makkah
quiz.scholar_reflection: He did not fly over the wall. He walked through the gate. The miracle was in what they could not see, not in what he could not do.

quiz.prompt: Abu Bakr feared. The Prophet ﷺ was certain. Both were in the same cave facing the same danger. What determines whether a situation produces fear or certainty?

options.text: Knowledge of Allah — those who know Him more deeply fear less
The Prophet ﷺ had direct knowledge of Allah's protection; Abu Bakr had faith but not certainty
Both responses were legitimate — fear in the face of danger is not weakness
Abu Bakr's love for the Prophet ﷺ made him fear for him more than for himself

quiz.citation: Quran 9:40 — 'Do not grieve, Allah is with us'
quiz.scholar_reflection: Abu Bakr's fear was not for himself — it was for the Prophet ﷺ. That is why the Prophet comforted him rather than rebuking him. His love made him afraid.

quiz.prompt: The Muhajirun left their homes, their property, their families, and their city. The Ansar received them and shared everything. Which sacrifice do you find more difficult — the giving up or the giving to?

options.text: Giving up what you have built is harder than sharing what you have
Receiving strangers into your home and treating them as brothers is the harder sacrifice
They are the same sacrifice — both require that something else matters more than comfort
The difficulty depends on what you are attached to

quiz.citation: Quran 59:9 — 'They give preference over themselves even when they are in need'
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Ansar are described in the Quran as preferring others over themselves. That preference — not wealth, not generosity of excess — is what made them Al-Ansar.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet ﷺ built his Masjid before his own house. What does this order of priorities tell you about what should come first in building a life or a community?

options.text: The communal space of worship precedes personal comfort
A community's spiritual centre is what everything else is built around
The Prophet ﷺ modelled that the house of Allah comes before the house of the nafs
All of these are contained in that sequence

quiz.citation: Account of the building of the Prophet's Masjid — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: He carried bricks. The Prophet himself, the Messenger of Allah, carried bricks to build a place of prayer. Not to supervise — to carry.

quiz.prompt: The Hijra established the principle: when you cannot practise your deen where you are, move toward where you can. How does this principle apply to your own life today?

options.text: Physically — are there places or situations I need to leave?
Socially — are there relationships that make my deen harder?
Internally — is there a migration of the heart away from what distances me from Allah?
All three levels of hijra are relevant — the scholars discuss all of them

quiz.citation: Quran 4:100 — 'Whoever emigrates in the cause of Allah will find many locations and abundance'
quiz.scholar_reflection: The scholars say there is an outer hijra and an inner one. The inner hijra is from what the nafs wants to what Allah wants. It is ongoing, every day.
